recall.define: For A C-subset compiler with original x86-64 and Thumb backends, define compiler token progress, literal admission bound, postfix lowering, unpublished parser scratch, subset semantic domain, modulo IR arithmetic, IR stack effect, verified IR consumption, IR terminal boundary, verified stack peak, leaf stack backend, emission transaction, Thumb leaf contract, argument retention register, defined-program differential test, translation evidence chain, giving each invariant.
recall.distinguish: For A C-subset compiler with original x86-64 and Thumb backends, distinguish these near concepts: compiler token progress versus parser progress; literal admission bound versus post-conversion range test; postfix lowering versus source evaluation order; unpublished parser scratch versus valid IR; subset semantic domain versus host C arithmetic; modulo IR arithmetic versus signed overflow; IR stack effect versus machine stack frame; verified IR consumption versus trusted parser output; IR terminal boundary versus first return encountered; verified stack peak versus measured stack use; leaf stack backend versus general calling backend; emission transaction versus partial output file; Thumb leaf contract versus all Arm targets; argument retention register versus callee-saved register; defined-program differential test versus arbitrary-source fuzzing; translation evidence chain versus matching final output.
recall.apply: Extend the IR to basic blocks, conditional branches, locals and calls, then prove each lowering preserves the expanded subset semantics. Compare representation choices with LLVM without using LLVM to implement the required pipeline.
